THE FAMILY BEHIND THE DEFENSE

The family & royal council

Choose a family member or adviser to help Celesteville. Each card explains its power. The battle pauses while you choose.

33 characters: the central book family, friends and adventure guests, alongside the original television, Badou and film roster. Book labels identify representative appearances. Powers and wartime roles are invented. Children provide civilian support; archive characters do not enter combat.

Field manual

Protect the palace and destroy Rataxes’s fortress in the northeast. Choose Story for more time to recover or Commander for stronger, faster assaults.

Supplies: provisioners collect physical caches and deliver to a supplied palace or home. Buildings connect within 360m. Enemy soldiers within 85m of a link cut it: isolated training runs at 25%. Clear raiders or build connecting homes. A provisioner’s Repair order costs 0.3 supplies per health.

Depot: hold the central depot with soldiers for 8 uncontested seconds. It grants 2 supplies per second and stops Basil’s reserve income. Destroy his Guard School to stop recruitment altogether. The reserve report is public convoy intelligence.

Construction: placing a structure assigns a free provisioner, preferring selected workers. It only progresses while a builder is on site. If the builder leaves or falls, send another with Repair. Extra builders do not speed up construction. Cancel unfinished structures for a 75% refund.

Research: an idle Guard School can research Cornelius’s coordinated volleys (150 supplies, 25s, +20% guard/scout damage). Artillery Works can calibrate shells (180 supplies, 35s, +25% gun damage). Research occupies that building, slows to 25% when isolated, and benefits existing and future troops. Cancellation refunds 75%; destruction loses the project.

Army: guards hold ground; scouts move quickly and see farther; field artillery outranges towers and deals 80% extra damage to buildings. Protect artillery with guards. Sandbag cover reduces incoming damage by 35% for either faction.

Commanders: select Babar and use Stand together (Q): 50 energy, 35s cooldown, +20 morale and 25% less incoming damage for friendly mobile units within 180m for 8s. Commanders start with 60 energy and recover 1.25/s, capped at 100. Rataxes can order a forced advance: nearby units move 30% faster and inflict 6 extra suppression per hit for 8s. His command requires a visible enemy and a supporting formation.

Morale: hits suppress units; below 25 they withdraw automatically. After 3 seconds without fire, morale recovers by 4/s, 12/s near a commander, or 10/s at an aid station. Below 45, movement and firing slow. Retreat moves 20% faster and avoids engagement.

Recovery: linked homes and palaces heal nearby units by 2/s after 5 seconds without fire; Celeste raises this to 6/s. Commanders recover for 45 seconds, then return when 100 supplies are available. Periwinkle reduces the wait to 25 seconds.

Orders: drag to select; Shift adds units; right-click moves or focuses a visible enemy. A selects attack-move, M move, G gather, E repair, S hold, R retreat. F2 selects the army; H returns to the palace. Hold Shift while giving orders, or enable Queue on touch, to append up to 16 waypoints. Hold and Retreat cancel the route. A queued order after gathering starts once the next delivery is complete. Ctrl/Command + 0–9 saves a control group; 0–9 recalls it; add Shift when saving to append. Select a production building and right-click (touch: Move then tap) to set its rally point. Rally provisioners to a cache to begin gathering. Space pauses. Touch uses the same explicit order buttons and Pan map. Scroll or +/− zooms. Family & council pauses the simulation; closing it restores the previous pause state.

Control groups

Assign the current selection, then recall it during battle. Fallen units are removed. Command is paused here.
